import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjectures associated with A113252

Corresponds to m = 6 in a family of 4th order linear recurrence sequences

This sequence is defined by the linear recurrence relation
a(n) = -4 a(n-1) + 144 a(n-3) + 1296 a(n-4) for n > 3.
Initial values are a(0) = -1, a(1) = 4, a(2) = 92, a(3) = 784.

*References:*
- [A113252](https://oeis.org/A113252)
-/

namespace OeisA113252

/--
a n is the sequence defined by the linear recurrence
$a(n) = -4 a(n-1) + 144 a(n-3) + 1296 a(n-4)$ with initial values $-1, 4, 92, 784$.
-/
def a : ℕ → ℤ
| 0 => -1
| 1 => 4
| 2 => 92
| 3 => 784
| n + 4 => -4 * a (n + 3) + 144 * a (n + 1) + 1296 * a n

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = -1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 4 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 92 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 784 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = -3856 := by rfl

/--
Conjecture: $a(m, 2n+1)$ is a perfect square for all $m, n$ (see A113249).
Specialized for $m=6$, which is A113252.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a113249-family-square-terms-lean/blob/9b999db08344184285e8050c2722c845fd5f5309/lean/OeisA113249FamilyFC.lean#L116-L124"]
theorem conjecture : ∀ n : ℕ, IsSquare (a (2 * n + 1)) := by
  sorry

end OeisA113252

review.notes:
Checked all seven declarations. The recurrence and initial values agree exactly with the source family at m = 6. The conjecture faithfully states the corresponding odd-indexed perfect-square claim over ℤ, including n = 0. Lean checks verified the source recurrence for every index greater than 3, the first 22 sequence values against OEIS, and squarehood of the first 12 odd-indexed terms.

The cited external proof compiled against the supplied checkout. Its exact target theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, with no sorryAx, supporting both the research solved category and the formal_proof record. OEIS still uses the word “Conjecture,” but this is not a status defect in the Lean file. OEIS entry pages returned HTTP 403; their full entry text was read through the official OEIS data mirror instead.
